name: Coiling vine
description:
A vine winding out across the floor, seen from above. Three runners off one point, each spiralling a different way and a different distance, because three copies of one spiral at 120 degrees is a pinwheel and this has to read as something that grew. The whole thing lies flat — every radius is squashed to 0.86, the camera's own angle — which is the difference between this and the sapling it replaces: that one stood up out of a hole and was most of a body tall, and what the weapon actually does happens on the ground. `meta.radius` is the coil's own reach and the game scales the sprite by `grabR / radius`, so the circle drawn and the circle that catches are now literally the same circle rather than two numbers held in agreement.

Dark all through: `$moss.dark2` for the cord with `$moss` along its lit edge, and the thorns `$blood.dark2` — a dark red against a dark green, which is the one pairing that keeps a barb readable at this size without lightening the plant. They lean back down the runner they sit on, because a barb pointing the way the vine grew is a spike and one pointing back is a hook, and this weapon holds things. Two leaves and no more: a coil hung with foliage stops being a cord.

`coil` is the arrival, and the reason the parts are cut into five segments a runner rather than drawn as one ribbon each. Each segment's points are held relative to its own start, so scaling it from nothing grows it out of where the last one ended instead of out of the middle of the picture; staggered along the runner with a `backOut` that throws each a little past full and settles it, that is an uncoil. Thorns and leaves ride the segment they grow on, so nothing appears before the vine under it. The clip is 0.3s, which is the weapon's own `riseS` — the two have to agree or the plant is still growing when it starts biting.

coil.description: coil — the ground breaks, the runners come up through it and wind out

evolved.description: Gold along the cord's lit edge and on the thorns, the mark every evolution in this arsenal wears. The body of the vine stays dark: a coil gilded through stops reading as a growing thing, and what the evolution changed is the grip, not the plant.
